title: Day of the Week
description:
Read a number from 1 to 7 and print the matching day name using a `switch` statement (1 = Monday ... 7 = Sunday).

For any other number, print `Invalid`.

Input: one integer `n`.
Output: the day name (e.g. `Wednesday`) or `Invalid`.

title: Vowel or Consonant
description:
Read a letter and say whether it is a vowel (a, e, i, o, u in either case) or a consonant. Use `switch` with grouped cases.

Input: one alphabetic character (read with `scanf(" %c", &ch)`).
Output: `Vowel` or `Consonant`.
constraints: The input is an English letter

title: Month Name
description:
Read a month number (1 to 12) and print its name (`January`, `February`, ... `December`). Print `Invalid` for any other number.

Input: one integer `m`.
Output: the month name or `Invalid`.

title: Simple Calculator
description:
Read two integers and an operator (`+`, `-`, `*`, `/`) and print the result. `/` is integer division. If the operator is `/` and the second number is 0, print `Error`. For any other operator, print `Invalid`.

Input: `a op b` separated by spaces (read the operator with `scanf(" %c", &op)`).
Output: the integer result, `Error` or `Invalid`.

title: Traffic Light
description:
Read a traffic light colour letter: `R` prints `Stop`, `Y` prints `Wait`, `G` prints `Go`. Any other letter prints `Invalid`.

Input: one character (read with `scanf(" %c", &ch)`).
Output: `Stop`, `Wait`, `Go` or `Invalid`.
constraints: The input is a single uppercase or lowercase letter

title: Grade Remark
description:
Print a remark for a grade letter: `A` -> `Excellent`, `B` -> `Good`, `C` -> `Average`, `D` -> `Poor`, `F` -> `Fail`. Any other character prints `Invalid`.

Input: one character (read with `scanf(" %c", &g)`).
Output: the remark.
constraints: The input is a single letter

title: Days in a Month
description:
Given a month number (1-12) print how many days it has, treating February as having 28 days. Use grouped `case` labels. Print `Invalid` for other numbers.

Input: one integer `m`.
Output: the number of days, or `Invalid`.

title: Digit to Word
description:
Read a single digit (0-9) and print it in words in lowercase: `zero`, `one`, ... `nine`. If the number is outside 0-9, print `invalid`.

Input: one integer `d`.
Output: the word.

title: Weekday or Weekend
description:
Read a day number (1 = Monday ... 7 = Sunday). Print `Weekend` for 6 and 7, `Weekday` for 1 to 5, and `Invalid` otherwise. Use fall-through case labels.

Input: one integer `n`.
Output: `Weekday`, `Weekend` or `Invalid`.

title: Compass Direction
description:
Read a direction letter and print its name: `N` -> `North`, `S` -> `South`, `E` -> `East`, `W` -> `West`. Accept both uppercase and lowercase. Otherwise print `Unknown`.

Input: one character (read with `scanf(" %c", &ch)`).
Output: the direction name or `Unknown`.
constraints: The input is a single letter

title: Quarter of the Year
description:
Months 1-3 are quarter 1, 4-6 quarter 2, 7-9 quarter 3, and 10-12 quarter 4. Given a month number, print `Q1`, `Q2`, `Q3` or `Q4`. Print `Invalid` for other numbers.

Hint: you can use `switch (m)` with grouped cases, or `switch ((m - 1) / 3)` for numbers 1-12.

Input: one integer `m`.
Output: the quarter or `Invalid`.

title: Restaurant Bill
description:
A menu has: 1 = Burger (80), 2 = Pizza (150), 3 = Pasta (120), 4 = Coffee (40). Given an item number and a quantity, print the total cost. For an item number not on the menu, print `Invalid item`.

Input: two integers `item quantity`.
Output: the total cost as an integer, or `Invalid item`.

title: Days in Month (Leap Year Aware)
description:
Given a month and a year, print the number of days in that month. February has 29 days in a leap year (divisible by 4, except centuries not divisible by 400), otherwise 28. If the month is not 1-12 print `Invalid`.

Input: two integers `month year`.
Output: the number of days or `Invalid`.

title: Unit Converter
description:
Convert a whole number value using a menu choice: 1 = kilometres to metres (x 1000), 2 = hours to minutes (x 60), 3 = kilograms to grams (x 1000), 4 = days to hours (x 24). For any other choice print `Invalid`.

Input: two integers `choice value`.
Output: the converted integer or `Invalid`.

title: Area of a Shape
description:
Choose a shape by code and print its area with exactly 2 digits after the decimal point.
- 1 = circle, input one integer radius `r`, area = 3.14159 * r * r
- 2 = rectangle, input `length width`, area = length * width
- 3 = triangle, input `base height`, area = 0.5 * base * height
For any other code print `Invalid`.

Input: the code on the first line, then the needed integers on the next line.
Output: the area formatted like `78.54`, or `Invalid`.

title: Shipping Cost
description:
Shipping has a base cost by zone: zone 1 = 50, zone 2 = 80, zone 3 = 120. Every kilogram above 5 kg costs an extra 10 (zone 1), 15 (zone 2) or 20 (zone 3). Print the total cost. For any other zone print `Invalid zone`.

Input: two integers `zone weight` (weight in whole kg).
Output: the total cost as an integer, or `Invalid zone`.

title: Operation Chain
description:
Start with the value 0. Read `n` operations; each is an operator character and an integer: `+ x` adds x, `- x` subtracts x, `* x` multiplies by x, `/ x` divides by x using integer division (skip the operation if x is 0), and any other operator is ignored. Print the final value.

Input: first `n`, then `n` lines each with `op x` (read op with `scanf(" %c", &op)`).
Output: the final integer value.
constraints: Intermediate values fit in a 64-bit integer

title: ATM Menu Simulation
description:
Simulate a simple ATM. Start with a balance read from input. Then read commands until the command `Q`:
- `D x`: deposit `x` (balance += x)
- `W x`: withdraw `x`; if `x` is more than the balance print `Insufficient` and leave the balance unchanged
- `B`: print the current balance
- `Q`: quit
- any other letter: print `Invalid`
Print every message on its own line.

Input: the starting balance, then commands (each read with `scanf(" %c", &cmd)`, followed by an integer for `D` and `W`). The last command is always `Q`.
Output: one line for each `B`, failed `W`, or invalid command.

title: Next Date
description:
Given a valid date, print the date of the next day. Handle month ends, year ends and leap-year February (29 days when the year is divisible by 4, except centuries not divisible by 400). Use a `switch` on the month to find its length.

Input: three integers `day month year`.
Output: the next date as `day month year` separated by single spaces.

title: Robot Commands
description:
A robot starts at (0, 0) facing North (North is +y, East is +x). Read command letters until `X`:
- `F`: move one step forward in the facing direction
- `B`: move one step backward
- `L`: turn 90 degrees left
- `R`: turn 90 degrees right
- any other letter is ignored
Print the final position and facing direction.

Input: a single string of uppercase letters, ending with `X` (read letters one by one with `scanf(" %c", &c)`).
Output: `x y Direction`, where Direction is `North`, `East`, `South` or `West`.
